 Advertisement Kansas midterm early voting sees early surge in Johnson, Douglas counties compared with 2022
 Advertisement Updated: 10:00 PM CDT Oct 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Nick Sloan Digital Content Producer Kansas midterm early voting sees early surge in Johnson, Douglas counties compared with 2022
 Updated: 10:00 PM CDT Oct 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Nick Sloan Digital Content Producer JOHNSON COUNTY, Kan. — Nearly twice as many people are voting early in Johnson County compared with the same point in the 2022 midterm election.
 The county recorded 37,798 early in-person voters during the first three days of voting, compared with 19,230 in 2022. 
 Advertisement That's a 97% increase.
 (Video above: No excuse early voting begins in Missouri) 
 Registered Democrats account for 54% of those early voters, compared with 33.3% for Republicans and 12.3% for unaffiliated voters.
 Those numbers reflect party registration, not votes for specific candidates. They also don't account for people who will vote later or on Election Day.
 Douglas County is seeing a similar increase.
 The county recorded 2,158 early in-person voters during its first three days, compared with 1,056 in 2022. That's a 104% increase.
 However, Douglas County has issued fewer mail ballots than it did four years ago, with 8,930 issued this year compared with 14,386 in 2022, a decrease of nearly 38%.
 In Wyandotte County, 3,547 people have voted through Tuesday, including 3,498 early in person and 49 by mail.
 Of the 4,220 mail ballots issued, nearly 72% went to registered Democrats, compared with 15% for Republicans and nearly 13% for unaffiliated voters.
 Wyandotte County's figures do not include a comparison with 2022.
